description: I'm developing Earth Symphony for NASA Space Apps 2026: an interactive platform that turns NASA Earth visualizations into sound and guided learning. My interests include web development, AI, Earth science, accessibility, and education. I'm seeking teammates skilled in data analysis, audio programming, UI/UX, Earth observation, and science communication. Join us to make our changing planet easier to explore, hear, and understand.
summary:
Earth Symphony is an interactive educational web application developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing The Earth Information Jukebox challenge.

It transforms NASA Earth Information Center visualizations into original soundscapes generated in real time. Visitors can explore Earth imagery, select environmental phenomena, and hear how the visual properties of scientific images change.

Our system maps image brightness, color saturation, spatial position, and differences between frames to different audio components.

The platform includes an interactive globe, NASA visualization library, synchronized image sequences, methodological explanations, and educational guidance.

Earth Symphony aims to make Earth science more engaging through visual, auditory, and interactive learning. Its current prototype sonifies rendered image properties, not calibrated environmental measurements or physical sounds recorded by satellites.
details:
The Problem

NASA's Earth Information Center provides scientific visualizations that help people explore changes in our planet. However, complex maps and animations can be difficult to interpret, especially for audiences without scientific training. Visual-only communication also limits multisensory exploration.

Our Solution

Earth Symphony is an interactive web platform that transforms NASA Earth visualization frames into dynamically generated sound.

Users can explore environmental phenomena such as precipitation, wind, temperature, and air quality, hear sonifications, and examine how the sounds are produced.

How It Works

The application processes visual properties of NASA-rendered images, including brightness, saturation, spatial position, and changes between frames.

These properties control audio parameters such as pitch, timbre, rhythm, and stereo position through the Web Audio API.

Users can explore images, navigate sampled frame sequences, adjust sound components, and review the transformation method.

Innovation

Earth Symphony combines scientific visualization, interactive sound synthesis, educational explanations, and transparent methodology in one accessible web experience.

Unlike a prerecorded musical video, the application allows visitors to interact with visual sources and explore the relationship between images and sound.

Technologies

HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Web Audio API, PHP, optional MySQL, and NASA Scientific Visualization Studio resources.

Expected Impact

Earth Symphony has potential applications in science education, museums, public outreach, and future accessible scientific communication.

Scientific Transparency

The current prototype sonifies properties of rendered images rather than original calibrated environmental measurements. It does not reproduce actual sounds recorded from Earth by satellites.

AI-Assisted Development

ChatGPT and AI-based tools supported software development, debugging, interface design, documentation, translation, and visual content creation. The application's sound is synthesized through programmed Web Audio API processes.
